lead_headline: Restaurant tracking catches fire: 6 fresh leads land today including Port Side's 10-year run ends in Five Points, Super Star Asian shutters after two decades in Athmar Park

restaurant.blurb: 6 leads today: Sandomi (Japanese sandos) at Edgewater, Marczyk FineBurger at Northfield opened; Port Side (10-year breakfast cafe), Super Star Asian (20-year Athmar Park staple), two Taco John's closures detected.

liquor.blurb: Day 40 of the application blackout. The licensing freeze that started June 1 just crossed the six-week mark with zero new filings detected today. Colorado's hospitality sector continues its unprecedented silence — 12,325 active licenses in the database, but not a single bar, restaurant, brewery, or retail application logged since early June. Historical patterns show post-holiday Tuesdays typically deliver 3-5 applications as developers return from long weekends. This morning: nothing. The drought now rivals the longest gaps ever recorded, and each passing day without activity deepens questions about whether this is bureaucratic backlog, capital flight, or structural shift in Colorado's liquor licensing ecosystem. The next application — whenever it lands — will break a streak that's already rewritten the baseline.

reputation.blurb: 10 mentions yesterday — the post-holiday bounce accelerates. Week closes at 64 mentions across 18 sources, down 15% from last week's 75 but recovering from Monday's holiday zero. Facebook leads again with 20 citations, Reddit adds 15, Denver Post contributes 8. Google News RSS captured 63 of 64 discoveries. Top stories: In-N-Out eyes Green Valley Ranch expansion, PNC closing 14 Colorado branches after FirstBank rebrand, downtown condo developer's property buy. The 10-mention Tuesday represents the strongest single-day pickup since before the July 4 holiday and suggests the compression was purely timing-driven. The 15% weekly decline now looks like typical holiday noise rather than trend shift — especially given yesterday's strong recovery and the quality of citations (major outlet pickups vs. social aggregation).

subscriptions.blurb: Net flat yesterday (1 new, 1 canceled) — the fifth consecutive zero-net day extends July's post-surge stall. MTD holds at +9 (+1.3/day), 90-day net at +118. The pattern solidifies: July opened strong with the June 29-30 carryover momentum (+17 in two days), added modest gains July 1-3 (+10 net), then froze completely (July 4-8: five straight flat days). The +1.3/day MTD pace now matches YTD baseline exactly — June's closing surge has been fully absorbed. Strip out June 29-30 and July runs at +0.1/day, essentially flat. The 7-day window (+9 net) looks healthier but only because it includes June 30's +13 spike. The stall mirrors June's mid-month doldrums when −9 weeks preceded the breakout, but there's no clear catalyst visible yet for a second surge.
